clue.text: Be insulting about upside-down cakes

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning a word upside-down means reading it from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: buns are small sweet cakes

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a tray of upside-down cakes.
explanation.walkthrough: BUNS read backwards gives SNUB. 'Upside-down cake' looks like a single bake, but 'upside-down' is the turnaround signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub somebody is to slight or rebuff them deliberately, an act of open rudeness.

clue.text: Anonymous place that may cause confusion

definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing for a noun: a thing that may cause confusion

blocks.note: grey means faceless, nondescript, as in a grey man
an area is a place or region

explanation.surface: A nameless spot that leaves visitors bewildered.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey area is a matter or situation that is unclear, without firm rules, so it breeds uncertainty.

clue.text: Tolerate sport

blocks.note: first meaning: put up with
second meaning: to have on or display, as in sporting a hat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' reads as a noun, a game, but here it is the verb meaning to show off something you have on.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the word means accept or stand for something, and also means to have clothing on the body.

clue.text: Criminal is to wind up trapped by proposal

indicators.note: something trapped is held inside, so these letters sit within the next piece

blocks.note: an offer is a proposal
to end is to wind up or finish

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker gets caught out by making a proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind up' suggests winding a clock or teasing someone; here it means bring to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: An offender is a person who has broken the law, a criminal or wrongdoer.

clue.text: Bachelor travels with newlyweds

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in a BA degree
rides means travels on horse or vehicle

explanation.surface: A single man goes on a trip in the company of a honeymooning couple.
explanation.definitionFit: Brides are women on or just after their wedding day, so they are among the recently married.

clue.text: Where high-fliers dine?

blocks.note: surface reading: an exclusive restaurant patronised by top executives
setter's reading: creatures that literally fly high, fed at a garden feeding platform

explanation.walkthrough: High-fliers suggests successful people at an expensive restaurant; read literally they are birds, and their dining spot is in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Bird tables are raised wooden platforms in gardens where food is put out for wild birds to eat.

clue.text: Mother almost sent back a smaller quantity of shellfish

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter
something sent back returns the way it came, so the word is read from the end

blocks.note: Mum is the British informal word for mother
less means a smaller amount

explanation.surface: Mum nearly returned some of the seafood she bought.
explanation.walkthrough: Mum is the everyday British word for mother; 'sent back' acts only on the smaller quantity, not on the mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A mussel is an edible bivalve mollusc with a dark elongated shell, a kind of shellfish.

clue.text: Reject vote for change

indicators.note: for change asks for the letters to be altered into another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A political slogan: turn down the ballot and campaign for change.
explanation.definitionFit: To veto a proposal is to refuse it formally, using an authority to block it.

clue.text: Hospital worker managed to move back to Southeast

indicators.note: moving back means going in the opposite direction, so the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: to run a business is to manage it
SE is the compass abbreviation for southeast

explanation.surface: A hospital employee arranged to relocate back to the south-east of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Managed' is a past tense, but the piece needed is the form that reads the same as the present: to run something is to manage it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurse is a trained carer who looks after patients on a ward, a staple employee of any hospital.

clue.text: Forthcoming about right to reject fashionable household goods

indicators.note: to reject something is to throw it back, so the following word is turned round
about means surrounding, so the first word wraps around the rest

blocks.note: the future is what is forthcoming, still to come
R is the abbreviation for right
in means fashionable, as in the in crowd

explanation.surface: Upcoming trends mean a fashionable home rejects its old fittings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forthcoming' reads as an adjective meaning open or frank; it stands for the time still to come, which wraps around the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Furniture means the chairs, tables, beds and similar movable items that equip a home.

clue.text: Lover got secret agent to consume fiery cocktail

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are mixed up
consuming something takes it inside, so the agent surrounds the other letters

blocks.note: James Bond is fiction's best-known secret agent
taken as written

explanation.surface: A romantic partner persuades a spy to down a fiery mixed drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiery cocktail' reads as one drink, but 'cocktail' is the signal to mix the letters of fiery, which sit inside BOND.
explanation.definitionFit: A boyfriend is a man in a romantic relationship with someone, so he is their lover or sweetheart.

clue.text: Is about to enter into celebration dance?

indicators.note: entering into something means going inside it, so these letters are placed within the next word

blocks.note: taken as written
C is short for circa, Latin for about
a do is an informal party or celebration

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a party is about to break into dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' looks like a phrase meaning soon; the words split, with 'about' giving the circa abbreviation and 'to' starting the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a party or club evening where people dance to recorded pop music.

clue.text: Material produced by least talented journalist

blocks.note: the worst is the least good or least able
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A news piece written by the paper's weakest reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' suggests copy for a newspaper; it is in fact cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Worsted is a smooth woollen yarn and the fine cloth woven from it, used for suits.

clue.text: Refuse to prepare a stew

indicators.note: to prepare a dish is to work the ingredients, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook declines to make a casserole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like the verb, decline; it is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste is unwanted matter thrown away, the same as refuse or rubbish.

clue.text: Fantastic to see emu and rodents running free

indicators.note: creatures running free scatter in no set order, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wildlife visitor delights in watching a big bird and some rats roaming loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremendous is used informally as praise meaning excellent or wonderful, like fantastic.

clue.text: Seafood makes nearly all collapse with convulsions

indicators.note: nearly all means everything bar the final letter is kept
convulsions are violent spasms, which throw these letters into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dodgy shellfish dish leaves almost everyone writhing in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: Collapse loses its last letter, and the remaining seven letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallop is an edible bivalve mollusc with a fan-shaped shell, eaten as a delicacy.

clue.text: Plane designed by experts

indicators.note: something designed is newly arranged, so these letters take a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An aircraft created by specialist engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel is a small group of specialists brought together to judge, advise or discuss.

clue.text: Humiliation of being hot in uniform

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the word that follows

blocks.note: uniform means all alike, the same
H for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: The embarrassment of sweating in a heavy school or army uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' looks like clothing; it is the adjective meaning unvarying.
explanation.definitionFit: Shame is the painful feeling of disgrace or embarrassment, the same as humiliation.

clue.text: Criticise artist quietly

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
p is the musical marking piano, meaning quietly

explanation.surface: A critic murmurs disapproval of a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: To rap someone is informal for rebuking them sharply, often in headlines, as in rapped by a judge.

clue.text: Mournful chap joined the scheme

blocks.note: a plan is a scheme
gent, short for gentleman, means a chap

explanation.surface: A sad fellow signed up to the project.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in the reverse of clue order: the scheme first, then the chap.
explanation.definitionFit: Plangent describes a loud, resonant sound with a sad or melancholy tone, a plaintive quality.

clue.text: Crowded into California city retreat

blocks.note: LA is Los Angeles, California's largest city
a den is a private retreat or hideaway

explanation.surface: People packed into a hideaway in Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means heavily loaded or burdened, so something laden is filled up, jammed or crammed.

clue.text: Gift one has to act in front of people

indicators.note: in front of says the first piece is placed before the second

blocks.note: to do is to act or perform
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A talented person must perform before an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gift' suggests a talent that must be shown off, but it is a present.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation is something given freely, especially money handed to a charity, so a gift or present.

clue.text: Beg to end nearly all pleasure

indicators.note: nearly all means one letter short of the whole, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: taken as written
a treat is a pleasure

explanation.surface: A plea to stop almost every kind of enjoyment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End' looks like a verb meaning stop; it is simply the word itself, trimmed by the deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to ask earnestly or plead with someone, the same as begging.

clue.text: Shock displayed amid utmost remorse

indicators.note: displayed amid means shown in the middle of the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Someone is jolted, showing deep regret.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a shaking movement, as of the earth or of a person in shock, a jolt.

clue.text: Root for vase in rubbish dump

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the second

blocks.note: a tip is British for a rubbish dump
an urn is a vase-shaped container

explanation.surface: Someone rummages through a landfill site for a discarded vase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Root for' looks like searching or cheering; 'Root' alone is the vegetable. A tip is the British word for a rubbish dump.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnip is a vegetable grown for its rounded white edible taproot, a classic root crop.

clue.text: Learns to play with a football team

indicators.note: to play with something is to fiddle with it, so these letters are moved around

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A youngster picks up the game by joining a soccer side.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a north London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a famous English Premier League football club, so it is a specific example of a team.

clue.text: Developed to ingest a basic foodstuff

indicators.note: ingesting something takes it inside, so the first word surrounds the next

blocks.note: bred means developed, as of a strain of animal or plant
taken as written

explanation.surface: An organism evolved to eat a staple food.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is the staple baked loaf of flour and water, long considered the most fundamental of foods.

clue.text: Make tea, or something stronger!

blocks.note: first meaning: to steep tea leaves in hot water
second meaning: a beer or other alcoholic drink, informally

explanation.surface: A host offers a cuppa, or perhaps a drink with alcohol in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to steep leaves for a hot drink, and the noun is informal for beer or other alcohol.

clue.text: Was sad about overwhelming desire engulfing teetotaller

indicators.note: engulfing means swallowing up, so these letters surround the following abbreviation

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
greed is an excessive, overpowering desire
TT is short for teetotal, one who drinks no alcohol

explanation.surface: Someone who doesn't drink was downcast about an urge that swallowed them up.
explanation.walkthrough: TT is the standard short form for teetotal, someone who never drinks alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: To regret something is to feel sorrow or remorse over it, to be unhappy at what happened.

clue.text: The point of blending teas?

indicators.note: blending mixes things together, so these letters are combined in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking the purpose of mixing different teas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The point' looks like 'the purpose'; it is a point of the compass.
explanation.definitionFit: East is one of the four cardinal compass points, as marked on a compass card.

clue.text: Appropriate time for musical performance

blocks.note: due means fitting or proper, as in due respect
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: The right moment for a concert piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A duet is a piece of music performed by two players or singers together.

clue.text: Social unrest doesn't start with Darwin's theory

indicators.note: not starting means the first letter is dropped

blocks.note: a revolution is a violent social upheaval

explanation.surface: Political turmoil fails to get going alongside a famous scientific idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Darwin set out the theory that species develop over generations through natural selection.

clue.text: Took item of women's clothing

blocks.note: first meaning: past tense of steal, took without permission
second meaning: a long scarf or wrap worn over the shoulders

explanation.surface: Someone helped themselves to a garment from a woman's wardrobe.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past tense of steal, meaning took dishonestly, and a noun for a shawl worn around the shoulders.
